title: A1 listening check
goal: Show that you can catch numbers, times, places and what people want in short, slow conversations, announcements and voicemails, including Canadian French speakers.

example.fr: Tu fais quoi en fin de semaine ?
example.en: What are you doing this weekend?

example.fr: Samedi, je vais magasiner au centre-ville.
example.en: On Saturday, I'm going shopping downtown.

example.fr: Le souper est à six heures.

items.note: In France, le dîner is the evening meal and le déjeuner is lunch.

example.fr: On mange ensemble pour le dîner, à midi.
example.en: We're eating together for lunch, at noon.

example.fr: Il y a un dépanneur au coin de la rue.
example.en: There's a convenience store at the corner of the street.

items.fr: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.

blocks.title: A1 listening: what you can do
blocks.body:
At A1, a listener can recognise **familiar words and very basic phrases** about themselves, their family and their surroundings, when people speak **slowly and clearly**. You can also catch the key information in short announcements and phone messages:

- **numbers and prices**
- **days and times**
- **places** (a room, a street, a shop)
- **what the speaker wants**: inviting, refusing, reminding, thanking

**How it works:** 14 items. For most of them, you hear one person speaking (a short message, a remark, an announcement or a voicemail), then choose the right answer. For 3 of them, you type exactly what you hear. Several speakers use **Canadian French**, as you will hear in Montréal, Gatineau or Moncton. Aim for **80%** to pass the checkpoint.

**For a fair score:** read the question *before* you play the audio, and try to play each recording **no more than twice**. In TEF and TCF Canada you often hear a recording only once. Use the slow button only if you are really stuck. The transcript appears after you answer.

steps.title: Part 1: Everyday conversations
steps.intro: Short messages and remarks from friends, neighbours and shop staff. Each recording has one speaker; the question tells you the situation.

blocks.fr: Salut, c'est Sofia ! Samedi, je vais magasiner au centre-ville avec ma sœur. Tu veux venir avec nous ? Bonne fin de semaine !
blocks.en: Hi, it's Sofia! On Saturday, I'm going shopping downtown with my sister. Do you want to come with us? Have a good weekend!
blocks.prompt: Sofia leaves you a message. What is she going to do on Saturday?
options: Go shopping downtown with her sister
Work downtown with her sister
Eat at a restaurant downtown with her sister
blocks.explain: [[Magasiner]] is Québec French for “to go shopping” (in France: [[faire les magasins]]). [[Bonne fin de semaine !]] = Have a good weekend! ([[fin de semaine]] is the usual Québec word; in France: [[le week-end]]).

blocks.fr: Tu veux venir souper chez moi samedi ? On mange vers six heures.
blocks.en: Do you want to come for supper at my place on Saturday? We eat around six.
blocks.prompt: What is the speaker inviting you to?
options: An evening meal at their place on Saturday, around 6 p.m.
Lunch at their place on Saturday, around noon
Breakfast at a café on Saturday, around 6 a.m.
blocks.explain: In Québec, [[souper]] is the evening meal (in France: [[dîner]]). [[Chez moi]] = at my place, [[vers six heures]] = around six. Supper means it is 6 in the evening.

blocks.fr: Un dépanneur ? Oui, il y a un dépanneur près d'ici : au coin de la rue, à côté de la banque.
blocks.en: A convenience store? Yes, there's a convenience store near here: at the corner of the street, next to the bank.
blocks.prompt: You ask a neighbour if there is a convenience store near here. Where is it?
options: At the corner of the street, next to the bank
Across from the bank, far from here
Behind the bank, on the next street
blocks.explain: A [[dépanneur]] is a Québec convenience store. [[Au coin de la rue]] = at the corner of the street; [[à côté de la banque]] = next to the bank.

blocks.en: You're welcome! Have a good day!
blocks.prompt: In a shop in Montréal, you say “Merci beaucoup !” to the clerk. She answers. What does she mean?
options: You're welcome, have a good day!
Welcome to Canada, see you soon!
Welcome to the shop, good evening!
blocks.explain: In Québec, [[Bienvenue !]] is a very common reply to [[merci]]: it means “You're welcome” (in France: [[De rien]] or [[Je vous en prie]]). Here it answers your thank-you. [[Bonne journée]] = have a good day ([[bonne soirée]] would be good evening).

blocks.fr: Un café et un muffin ? Alors, ça fait six dollars cinquante, s'il vous plaît.
blocks.en: A coffee and a muffin? So, that comes to six dollars fifty, please.
blocks.prompt: The cashier tells you the price. How much do you pay?
blocks.explain: [[six dollars cinquante]] = $6.50 (written 6,50 $ in Québec). [[Six]] is one short syllable; 16, [[seize]], has a z sound in it.

blocks.fr: J'habite à Gatineau avec ma famille.
blocks.explain: [[J'habite]]: je becomes j' before a vowel or a silent h. [[Gatineau]] ends in -eau, which sounds like “o”.

blocks.fr: Désolée, je ne peux pas venir ce soir. Je travaille jusqu'à vingt-deux heures.
blocks.en: Sorry, I can't come tonight. I'm working until 10 p.m.
options: Saying no to an invitation because of work
Accepting an invitation for tonight
Asking what time the party starts
blocks.explain: [[Désolée, je ne peux pas venir]] = Sorry, I can't come: a refusal. The reason is work, until 22 h (10 p.m.).

blocks.fr: Nous allons au parc demain matin.
blocks.explain: Futur proche: [[nous allons]] + place. [[Au parc]] = à + le parc. The s of [[allons]] is silent here.

steps.title: Part 2: Announcements and voicemails
steps.intro: Listen for the key information: a time, a number, a day, a place, and why the person is speaking.

blocks.fr: Mesdames et messieurs, bonsoir. Le magasin ferme dans quinze minutes, à vingt et une heures. Merci et bonne soirée !
blocks.en: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. The store closes in fifteen minutes, at 9 p.m. Thank you and have a good evening!
blocks.prompt: What time does the store close?
options: 9 p.m.
blocks.explain: [[à vingt et une heures]] = at 21 h, 9 p.m. [[Dans quinze minutes]] (in fifteen minutes) tells you it is now 8:45.

blocks.fr: Attention, s'il vous plaît. Ce soir, le cours de français est dans la salle dix-huit, pas dans la salle huit. Merci !
blocks.en: Attention, please. Tonight, the French class is in room eighteen, not in room eight. Thank you!
options: Room 18
Room 8
Room 80
blocks.explain: [[dans la salle dix-huit, pas dans la salle huit]]: room 18, not room 8. [[Pas]] tells you which room is wrong.

blocks.fr: Bonjour, c'est Karim, de la clinique Saint-Denis. Je vous appelle pour votre rendez-vous avec le docteur Roy : c'est jeudi à dix heures trente. Si vous ne pouvez pas venir, appelez la clinique, s'il vous plaît. Merci, bonne journée !
blocks.en: Hello, this is Karim from the Saint-Denis clinic. I'm calling about your appointment with Dr. Roy: it's on Thursday at 10:30. If you can't come, please call the clinic. Thank you, have a good day!
options: To remind you about your appointment
To cancel your appointment
To ask you to work on Thursday
blocks.explain: [[Je vous appelle pour votre rendez-vous]]… [[c'est jeudi]]: he gives you the day and time. That is a reminder. You call back only [[si vous ne pouvez pas venir]] (if you can't come).

blocks.fr: Bonjour, c'est Karim, de la clinique Saint-Denis. Je vous appelle pour votre rendez-vous avec le docteur Roy : c'est jeudi à dix heures trente. Si vous ne pouvez pas venir, appelez la clinique, s'il vous plaît. Merci, bonne journée !
blocks.en: Hello, this is Karim from the Saint-Denis clinic. I'm calling about your appointment with Dr. Roy: it's on Thursday at 10:30. If you can't come, please call the clinic. Thank you, have a good day!
options: Thursday at 10:30
Tuesday at 10:30
Thursday at 12:30
blocks.explain: [[jeudi]] = Thursday ([[mardi]] = Tuesday). [[dix heures trente]] = 10:30; 12:30 would be [[midi et demi]] or [[douze heures trente]].

blocks.fr: Salut, c'est Raj ! Pour le dîner demain, rendez-vous au restaurant à midi, en face du métro Mont-Royal. Appelle-moi sur mon cellulaire. Bye !
blocks.en: Hi, it's Raj! For lunch tomorrow, let's meet at the restaurant at noon, across from Mont-Royal metro. Call me on my cell. Bye!
blocks.prompt: When and where are they meeting?
options: At noon, at a restaurant across from Mont-Royal metro
At noon, inside Mont-Royal metro station, next to a restaurant
In the evening, at a restaurant next to the metro
blocks.explain: In Québec, [[le dîner]] is lunch, and [[à midi]] (at noon) confirms it. [[En face du métro]] = across from the metro. Raj also uses two Québec words: [[cellulaire]] (cellphone; France: [[portable]]) and [[Bye !]], an informal Québec goodbye borrowed from English (for recognition; use [[Salut !]] or [[À demain !]] yourself).

blocks.fr: Il fait froid aujourd'hui, mais il fait beau.
accept: Il fait froid aujourd'hui mais il fait beau.
blocks.explain: Weather uses [[il fait]] + adjective. [[Aujourd'hui]] has an apostrophe in the middle.

summary:
- Catch prices, room numbers, days and times in short announcements and voicemails
- Understand why someone is speaking: inviting, refusing, reminding, thanking
- Recognise Canadian French you will hear every day: [[fin de semaine]], [[magasiner]], [[souper]], [[dîner]], [[dépanneur]], [[Bienvenue !]]

meta.author: ai
meta.notes: Rewrote l1, l3, l4, l5 as single-speaker recordings (one voice no longer reads two people); removed the non-homophone accept 'On va au parc…' from dictation l8; labelled Bye ! as informal Québec usage.
